notes: HEB800 web depth. Large, high-contrast against sky; robust at long standoff.
Bar diameter B450C. Dense cages self-occlude heavily; individual bar counting is far harder than cage presence.
Nelson stud shank diameter.
Surface class, not an object; presence is near-trivial, condition is not.
M24 shank. Only the protruding end is visible once installed.
M24 nut across flats.

CRITICAL: once the nut is torqued, only the 4 mm washer edge annulus is visible, and only from a near-tangential viewpoint. The highest self-occlusion prior in the vocabulary and the reason IR-P4-019 is the canonical insufficient-evidence case.
Defect class: requires resolving thread protrusion differential, i.e. a sub-feature of the bolt itself.
Defect class defined by an empty hole; strongly confusable with an occluded bolt.
Primary evidence class for edge protection (IR-P3-008) and work-zone delimitation (IR-P1-002).
New Jersey type; also evidence for IR-P6-032.
Presence is detectable; legibility of the sign face is not, which is what the regulation actually requires.
Hands are occluded by the task being performed more often than not.
Most reliable PPE class: high on the body, high contrast, rarely self-occluded.
Feet are occluded by terrain, spoil heaps, formwork and other workers in most site imagery.
Retroreflective, large; the most reliable PPE evidence after helmet.
Mesh fencing; low texture contrast against background is the main failure mode, not size.
Plural duplicate of OC-07 in the trained vocabulary; merge before use and report the merge.
Duplicate of OC-06 in the trained vocabulary; merge before use and report the merge.
Portable ladder. Long, high-contrast, linear; presence is easy. Whether it is secured is not a property of the ladder and cannot be read from a detection of it.

Fall-arrest harness. Worn against the torso and routinely hidden by outer clothing, the worker's back and the task; the karabiner that actually makes it protective is smaller still. Lowest base recall in the PPE group and the limiting component of IR-P3-035.
Timber dunnage under stored steel. Load-bearing and therefore covered by its own load; visible only in the gap between the stack and the ground, from a low viewpoint.
Steel or timber spreader plate under a crane outrigger. Two of four are always behind the machine body; ground-level standoff also foreshortens the pad to a thin edge.
Whole-machine class. Trivially detectable and therefore of no evidential value on its own; it serves only to anchor the outrigger sub-checks of IR-P4-037.
Edge protection at the head of an excavation or ladder landing. Alternative collective measure that discharges the harness requirement of IR-P3-035.
Prohibited condition class for IR-P4-036. Specular and highly illumination-dependent; wet ground and standing water are frequently confused, so a positive detection is weaker than usual.
